authoritative: Source: the Lieutenant Governor's official general election report, whose county rows add up to each candidate's printed state total; they replace Algara and Amlani's county rows.
title: General election report by county, Utah, November 3, 1998

pages.hint: One row per Utah county with its registered voters and number voting, then one column per candidate across the page, in printed order, with the candidate's name as the header; read the votes only, never the percent row, and leave a cell empty when it is blank. Include the TOTAL row. Columns of state legislative races, judges, and other offices may appear: keep them with their printed headers.

One row per Utah county with its registered voters and number voting, then one column per candidate across the page, in printed order, with the candidate's name as the header; read the votes only, never the percent row, and leave a cell empty when it is blank. Include the TOTAL row. Columns of state legislative races, judges, and other offices may appear: keep them with their printed headers. This page prints no county names: the 29 rows below the headings are the counties in this fixed order: Beaver, Box Elder, Cache, Carbon, Daggett, Davis, Duchesne, Emery, Garfield, Grand, Iron, Juab, Kane, Millard, Morgan, Piute, Rich, Salt Lake, San Juan, Sanpete, Sevier, Summit, Tooele, Uintah, Utah, Wasatch, Washington, Wayne, Weber. Use those names as the row labels, followed by the Total row.
